newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end sharply lower despite trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end sharply lower despite trade surplus.

text.p: Malaysian shares continued on their downward trend on Tuesday, dragged down by foreign institutional selling as investors remained uncertain of where the market would bottom-out, dealers and analysts said.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalises stocks closed down 15.35 points, or 1.43 percent, to 1,059.51, after reaching a session low of 1,056.30.
"Malaysia still looks good fundamentally, it's just sentiment that's not positive at the moment," said a strategist at a foreign brokerage house in Kuala Lumpur.

A trade surplus for February of 367.2 million ringgit, compared to a deficit of 102.9 million ringgit in January failed to inspire share prices, analysts said. The figures were released earlier on Tuesday.
The blue-chip index's closing level was its lowest for nearly nine months.
"There has been a sell program in the market since this morning, and there are no buyers. Sentiment is very weak," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage.
Volume remained thin with 245 million shares traded, valued at 1,549 million ringgit. Losers thumped gainers 553 to 84.
